svg.text: The request: the agent's tools/call with the user's own token (T2) and the tool arguments. Every governed call meets the four walls in this order (the private MCP server has no Wall 1).
What it checks
Decision inputs
Deny shape
Where the denial is logged
Controls that change the answer
The prompt, the model's output and the tool result,
against content-safety classes: jailbreak, indirect attack
(in the prompt and after a tool call), hate, sexual,
violence and self-harm at Medium. Protected material is
flagged, not blocked.
The text, and the guardrail's categories and
severity thresholds. Not the user's token or
roles.
The run stops, and the Foundry span carries error.type =
content_filter. A preview control that fires on only some
attacks, so the walls below never rely on it.
Application Insights spans (invoke_agent, chat).
Sentinel ABW-008 when it stops a run. Join key:
the trace id only, no request_id.
Wall 0: Foundry
guardrail (detective)
Tool allow-list. allowed_tools names the only
tools the model may call on each server, and
require_approval is always on for
actions.place_order.
A valid Entra token for this MCP server: signature,
audience, tenant. Then who and what: kill switch, client
allow-list, scope, role. Then volume: 120 calls a minute
per user.
Token claims: aud, tid, oid, azp, scp, roles. The
named values abw-deny-oids and
abw-allowed-azp. A counter per oid; the
JSON-RPC method.
401 unauthorized with a fixed message. 403 forbidden
with a reason (revoked, client_not_allowed,
missing_scope or missing_role) plus the request_id. 429
when rate limited.
ApiManagementGatewayLogs (RequestId), the
abw-gateway trace and the
abw-gateway-decisions metric. Sentinel
Wall 1: APIM gateway
Kill switch. Put a user's oid in abw-deny-oids
and the gateway refuses that person on every
gateway API within 45-90 s. The private MCP
server is outside the gateway, so outside the
kill switch.
The token again, because the server does not rely on
the gateway: signature, audience, issuer, tenant, azp,
scope. Then the tool: tools/list is filtered by role, and
tools/call needs the role and passes the tool's own rule.
Token claims (roles, scp, azp, oid), the tool
arguments, and the rule: the project must be in
the roles, the ticker must not be on the restricted
list.
401 or 403 with a reason code, or HTTP 200 with
decision DENIED: a soft denial the agent reads as a
result. Also NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENT and
obo_failed.
An audit event (tool_denied, auth_failed,
wall_violation_attempt, order_blocked): console
JSON, Application Insights and the WORM audit
blob. Sentinel ABW-001, ABW-002.
Wall 2: MCP server
Client allow-list. abw-allowed-azp admits only
the agent client, the test client and the Azure
CLI client at the gateway, and the MCP
server checks azp again.
The data plane's own roles, on the user's own token T4
rather than the server's identity: Azure RBAC for the
blob container and the Search index, Cosmos DB's
data-plane roles for the Cosmos DB container.
T4 (oid = the user) and the user's groups:
sg-abw-wall-falcon, sg-abw-traders,
sg-abw-compliance, sg-abw-research.
403 from the data service. For Storage the MCP server
reports storage_rbac_denied.
StorageBlobLogs (ClientRequestId). Search and
Cosmos DB logs are matched by time. Sentinel
ABW-007: gateway and MCP allowed, storage
denied.
Wall 3: data plane
Group membership. People get data access
only through groups, and the operator holds
no data role of its own. Leave the group and
Wall 3 refuses, even while the token still
carries the role (the drift ABW-007 watches).
Data: reached only when
all four walls say yes
Stops at Wall 1. Ian has no app roles: the gateway answers 403 missing_role to every
tools/call behind it, and no tool runs.
Stops at Wall 2. Wes asks for an Orion memo: the gateway lets Wall.Falcon through, the
MCP server answers project_not_in_token_roles, and Storage is never touched.
Stops at Wall 3. A user holds the Wall.Falcon role but is not in sg-abw-wall-falcon: the
gateway and the MCP server allow it, Storage answers 403 (Sentinel ABW-007).

Azure Policy (initiative abw-agent-platform-controls) is not a wall: it decides what may exist, not what a request may do. Five control families: no keys, private data planes, approved tools and models, guardrails attached, hygiene. A custom Deny refuses Foundry connections to MCP
targets that are not approved.
Authorization layers: four walls, each with its own deny
What each wall checks, what it decides on, what a denial looks like, where it is logged
Agents Behind the Wall - diagram 05 of 13 - generated by docs/diagrams/build_diagrams.py
Legend
Identity (Entra ID)
Network, API gateway (APIM)
Compute (agents, MCP servers)
Data stores
Observability
Deny, risk, kill switch
Human / optional (dashed)
Azure Policy, governance
People, client tools
Allowed flow
Denied exit / risk path
Manual step (dashed)
What to notice
- Each wall is a different system with its own deny, so getting past one still meets the next.
- Wall 2 checks the token again instead of trusting the gateway, and Wall 3 decides on the user's own token T4, never on the server's
identity for user data (the restricted-list read and the audit append use it).
- Wall 0 is detective and best effort (a preview control). The three identity walls, 1, 2 and 3, make a call safe.
Numbered flow
1. Request reaches Wall 0: the Foundry guardrail screens the content.
2. It passes to Wall 1: the gateway checks token, role, rate and kill switch.
3. It passes to Wall 2: the MCP server re-checks the token and applies the tool's rule.
4. It passes to Wall 3: the data plane's own roles answer for the user.
5. Only when all four walls say yes does the call reach the data.
